correctness.rationale: Each labelled token must switch the edge endpoints, giving a baseline 2s moves. A crossing external excursion uses an alternate path of length at least g-1, costing at least g-2 beyond baseline. With no crossing, initial saturation forces a return excursion, after which the initially moved token remains on its wrong starting endpoint and both endpoints are full, so a second return excursion is necessary: at least four extra moves. A 2-token buffer construction gives exactly 2s+4; a shortest cycle bypass construction gives exactly 2s+g-2. Both enforce capacity at every move for every s>=2. Exact BFS on 46 finite host/edge/capacity instances independently confirms both cases; finite tests do not replace proof.

value.rationale: Identifies the exact unavoidable congestion overhead for a basic two-full-site exchange in the current labelled-token graph family, uniformly over all finite connected hosts. The local cycle threshold g=3,4,5,>=6 or bridge supplies an interpretable structural classification and complements the open odd-cycle diameter problem without claiming its resolution. Infinite domain and precise edge dependence make it more than a single numerical or routine small case.
